title: In Psalms 31 What Does It Mean To Truly Trust In God During Difficult Times
paragraphs: Introduction: Trusting God When Life Hurts

The journey of faith is often marked by seasons of difficulty and distress. Psalm 31 offers a profound exploration of what it means to truly trust in God during life’s hardest moments. Written by David, this psalm models a deeply personal conversation with the Lord amid suffering, betrayal, and uncertainty. Through David’s words, believers are invited to anchor their hope in the steadfast character and promises of God.
David’s Circumstances: A Context of Crisis

David likely composed Psalm 31 in a time of acute danger—possibly on the run from Saul or facing betrayal by those he trusted. His expressions of fear, slander, and isolation resonate with anyone who has faced overwhelming trials. Notice his opening plea:
In thee, O Jehovah, do I take refuge; Let me never be put to shame: Deliver me in thy righteousness. - Psalm 31:1 ASV
David’s first instinct is to seek refuge in God. Trust, in biblical terms, means turning to God as a safe place, believing He alone can deliver and vindicate.
The Nature of True Trust in God
Trusting God, especially in hardship, is not passive resignation, but an active reliance on His character and promises:

Trust is Personal: David addresses God directly: “Into thy hand I commend my spirit” (Psalm 31:5 ASV). This is a personal surrender, echoed by Jesus on the cross (Luke 23:46 ASV), showing ultimate trust even in death.

Trust is Rooted in God’s Faithfulness: David recalls God’s past faithfulness (“thou hast redeemed me, O Jehovah, thou God of truth” - Psalm 31:5 ASV). Remembering God’s unchanging nature strengthens present trust.

Trust Endures Despite Fear: David does not hide his fear and distress (“For my life is spent with sorrow, and my years with sighing” - Psalm 31:10 ASV). True trust does not deny pain but brings it honestly before God.

Trust Leads to Action: David chooses not to take matters into his own hands but commits his future to God: “But I trusted in thee, O Jehovah: I said, Thou art my God. My times are in thy hand” (Psalm 31:14-15 ASV).
God’s Response to Trust
Throughout Psalm 31, David’s trust is not misplaced. He experiences God’s steadfast love and deliverance:
Oh how great is thy goodness, which thou hast laid up for them that fear thee, Which thou hast wrought for them that take refuge in thee, before the sons of men! - Psalm 31:19 ASV
Even when immediate circumstances do not change, the assurance of God’s goodness and presence transforms David’s outlook. He ends the psalm with a call for all believers:
Be strong, and let your heart take courage, All ye that hope in Jehovah. - Psalm 31:24 ASV
New Testament Insights: Trust in Christ

The New Testament deepens this theme. Jesus Himself quoted Psalm 31:5 as He died, perfectly modeling trust in the Father’s plan even in suffering. For believers today, trust rests on the finished work of Christ:
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God. - Ephesians 2:8 ASV
Trusting God involves believing in His promise of salvation through Jesus, confident that He is always working for our good (Romans 8:28 ASV).
Application: Learning to Trust God Practically
Pray Honestly: Bring your fears, doubts, and pain to God as David did.
Remember God’s Faithfulness: Recall past experiences of God’s help, and meditate on His promises.
Commit Your Future: Entrust your life and circumstances to God’s sovereign care.
Encourage Others: Just as David exhorted others, share testimonies of God’s faithfulness to strengthen fellow believers.
Conclusion: The Heart of Trust

Trusting God in difficult times does not mean the absence of fear, but the presence of faith—faith that God is good, sovereign, and loving, even when we cannot see the way ahead. As Psalm 31 reveals, such trust is not only possible but brings hope, courage, and peace in the storms of life.
